definition: to stop doing something before it is finished, or to leave it completely

collocations.example: The company abandoned the project after costs rose sharply.
Management decided to abandon the idea of a new office.

definition: to take in a liquid or gas

collocations.example: This material absorbs water very quickly.
Silica gel packs absorb moisture inside the box.

definition: based on general ideas rather than real or physical things

collocations.example: Freedom is an abstract concept that is hard to define.
The professor explained the abstract idea with a simple example.

definition: existing in large amounts; more than enough

collocations.example: The region has an abundant supply of clean water.
The country has abundant natural resources.

definition: to happen faster, or to make something happen faster

collocations.example: The new policy is designed to accelerate economic growth.
We used new software to accelerate the hiring process.

definition: the right or chance to use or enter something

collocations.example: Only authorized staff can gain access to the server room.
All students have access to the online library.

definition: to have or provide enough space for someone or something

collocations.example: The hotel can accommodate up to 300 guests.
The conference hall can accommodate a large group.

definition: to go somewhere together with someone

collocations.example: An assistant will accompany the visitor during the tour.
A teacher must accompany the group on the trip.

definition: to succeed in doing or finishing something

collocations.example: She accomplished her sales goal ahead of schedule.
The team accomplished the task on time.

definition: an arrangement that lets you keep money at a bank

collocations.example: I would like to open an account at this bank.
She transferred her salary into her bank account.
